meta.titulo: Terra Viva — the living calendar of your land
meta.descricao: Decision support for farmers in Angola: NASA data for your area, indicators with visible rules, and a comparison of three crop rotations.

a11y.mapa: Map of Angola with the eight preloaded farming areas

hero.etiqueta: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Calumbo, Zango local event
hero.sub: Pick your area, what you planted and what matters to you. You see the land's year and three rotations to compare.
hero.motivoLegenda: The Earth Clock — one year in your area, month by month
hero.subMais: Pick your area, say what you planted and what matters to you. Terra Viva reads NASA data for your point on the map, shows the year of your land month by month, and compares three crop rotations — with the evidence, the gaps and the risks in plain sight.

confianca.sub: Every value on screen carries one of three labels. They are never mixed.

nasa.texto: Rain, temperature, soil moisture and radiation for your point, as the satellite records them.

calculado.texto: Indicators derived from the data, with the rule written beside them.

conhecimento.texto: Crop cycles and needs, always with the source.

fluxo.titulo: From your field to the comparison
fluxo.sub: Four big taps. You can go back whenever you like.

passo1.sub: Tap the map or pick the area from the list.
passo1.nenhuma: You have not chosen an area yet.
passo1.fonteMapa: Outline: Natural Earth (public domain). Coordinates: OpenStreetMap / Nominatim (ODbL).

solo.sub: Pick the texture of your soil. You can change it later.
solo.nota: This information comes from you, not from a satellite. The satellite sees rain, temperature, moisture, vegetation and relief — it does not see soil fertility.

passo2.sub: Pick last season's crop. The one before is optional.
passo2.ajuda: If you left the land to rest, choose “Fallow”. You don't need to know the variety name.

passo3.sub: Say what matters most: water, yield, soil or risk.
passo3.nota: The “yield” priority is recorded but does not change the score yet: there is no yield data per crop. Nothing is estimated in its place.

passo4.sub: Three rotations for the same area and the same priorities.
passo4.semZona: Choose the area in step 1 first.
passo4.semCultura: Choose last season's crop in step 2 first.
passo4.aCaminho: Change the rain scenario in the clock and watch the scores move.

clima.titulo: The year of the land in this area
clima.semZona: Choose an area to see the numbers for the year.
clima.carregando: Reading NASA data for this area…
clima.erro: Could not load the data for this area.
clima.limite: These numbers come from a NASA model for a point on the map, not from your field. The rules and limits are on the About page.
clima.qualidade: One month in this series was flagged as suspect and left out of the averages.

relogio.sub: Three rings: rain, soil moisture and temperature, month by month. The inner ring is the calendar of the chosen crop.
relogio.resumo: Rain {chuva} mm · season {inicio}–{fim} · {n} months of bare soil
relogio.aria: Earth Clock: twelve months of rain, soil moisture and temperature, with the calendar of the chosen crop.
relogio.atrasoNota: With the rain delayed, the season now starts in {mes}.
relogio.aviso: This scenario was also applied to the scores below.
relogio.regra: Rings: each month is a sector, with height proportional to the value (rain in mm; soil and temperature relative to the local maximum and minimum). Crops: they start in the month the rainy season begins and last the shortest EcoCrop cycle; the faded part runs to the longest cycle. Months without a crop are bare soil. Because the EcoCrop cycle range is wide (maize: 65 to 365 days), the solid arc uses the middle of the range and the faded part runs to the longest cycle; each crop's sheet has both limits.
relogio.regraCenario: The scenarios change rain only: soil moisture and temperature stay as measured, because we have no model that links them reliably.
relogio.frase: Rain here falls from {inicio} to {fim}. For the other {n} months the field has no crop.
relogio.fraseUm: Rain here falls from {inicio} to {fim}. Only 1 month has no crop.

resultado.nota: The score compares the three rotations with each other. It is not a harvest forecast.

notas.maoDeObra: Labour does not change the score: we have no data on work requirements per crop. It is noted for local validation.
notas.irrigacao: You have irrigation, so water weighs less in the score.
notas.sequeiro: Without irrigation, water weighs more in the score.

resultado.erro: Could not build the rotations with the data for this area.

regrasTexto.metodo: Each crop scores 0 to 1 on every available criterion. The rotation is the weighted average of those criteria (80%) plus family diversity (20%), rounded to 100.
regrasTexto.semDados: Left out for lack of data: soil cover, organic matter and yield. No value is estimated in their place.

resultado.sinaisNota: Signals we calculate from the criteria. 0.75 or more = Good.
resultado.resumo: {qual} scores highest for your priorities: {nota} of 100.

porque.atual: This is the sequence you gave, repeated as it is: {c1}, {c2}, {c3}. It is the baseline for the comparison.
porque.leguminosa: {cultura} is a legume and comes after {anterior}: it puts nitrogen back into the soil without extra fertiliser.
porque.diversidade: The three seasons are from different families, which helps break the pest cycle.
porque.semRepeticao: No crop repeats in two seasons in a row.

beneficio.azoto: One legume season puts nitrogen back into the soil.
beneficio.pragas: The family changes between seasons, so pest pressure drops.
beneficio.agua: The area's rain falls within the range these crops tolerate.
beneficio.diversidade: Three different families across the cycle.
beneficio.estabilidade: A sequence without sharp changes in demand between seasons.

sobre.intro: Terra Viva was born at the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, at the Calumbo, Zango local event. It is a decision-support tool: it helps farmers and extension officers think through crop rotation, it does not decide for them.
sobre.metodo: Each area has a verified reference point. For that point we download NASA POWER observations — temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, radiation and wind — over several decades, and aggregate them by month and by year. From that series we calculate simple indicators: start and end of the rainy season, consecutive dry days, months with bare soil, heat stress and variation between years. Each indicator carries the CALCULATED BY US label and the written rule, because the rule is our choice.
sobre.limites: The satellite does not measure soil fertility. It measures rain, temperature, moisture, vegetation and relief. The crop sheets cover wide ranges, not the variety in your field. Market prices are not included. That is why every rotation shows the “What we don't know” panel and the list of what needs local validation.
sobre.h2dados: Data we use and data we don't
sobre.dados: We use NASA POWER as the main source, with supporting global sources (FAO and, where accessible, ISRIC SoilGrids). The United States–based challenge resources — WSS, CDL, PRISM, SSURGO, NAIP — do not cover Angola and are therefore not used. The decision is recorded here to be discussed, not hidden.
sobre.ia: The tool does not use AI to generate recommendations: the texts for each rotation are written by deterministic rules from the engine's results. Generative AI was used while developing this site (code, text and design), with the team reviewing it. No number shown was generated by AI.
sobre.privacidade: No accounts, no server, no personal data collected. Your choices stay on your phone.

fontesPagina.intro: Everything on screen comes from somewhere. This is the list, with licence and date consulted.
fontesPagina.nasa: NASA POWER — Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources. Weather and energy parameters by coordinates, no API key. Main climate source.
fontesPagina.fao: FAO — crop water requirements and crop sheets. Used through the EcoCrop database, cited field by field.
fontesPagina.ecocrop: FAO EcoCrop — ecological requirements of crops: family, cycle, temperature, annual rainfall and use. It is the basis of the eight crop sheets; fields the database does not cover stay as missing data.
fontesPagina.soilgrids: ISRIC SoilGrids — global soil at 250 m. Not integrated yet; see “possible improvement”.
fontesPagina.naturalearth: Natural Earth — outline of Angola, 1:110m scale, public domain.
fontesPagina.osm: OpenStreetMap and Nominatim — coordinates of the eight areas. ODbL licence.
fontesPagina.fraunces: Fraunces, by Undercase Type — headings. SIL Open Font License 1.1, self-hosted as WOFF2.
fontesPagina.karla: Karla, by Jonny Pinhorn — body text. SIL Open Font License 1.1, self-hosted as WOFF2.
fontesPagina.spaceapps: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — challenge and context of the Calumbo, Zango local event.
